ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.global_contrast_ratio: Predominantly low-intensity (black/dark-grey) background with approximately 20-25% high-intensity (white) localized pixel coverage in annular and circular patterns.
ventral_fluke_pixel_intensity_distributi.spatial_color_mapping: High-contrast white annular rings and solid circular spots distributed across the medial and distal regions of both fluke lobes, with highest density concentrated in the inner-medial quadrants.

trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.median_notch_angle: Deep V-shaped depression with an approximate aperture of 42 degrees and a vertex depth comprising roughly 15% of the total vertical height of the fluke visible above the waterline.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.edge_topography_serration_map: High-frequency serration along the continuous trailing edge; pixel-amplitude variations are most pronounced on the medial sections, characterized by sharp peaks and deep narrow valleys.
trailing_edge_2d_geometric_contour.lobe_sweep_trajectory: Strongly convex trajectory along the trailing edge, tapering to sharp, upward-pointing distal tips (apexes).

localized_surface_anomalies.rosette_scar_constellations: Widespread spatial detection of white annular (ring-like) high-contrast pixel clusters across the entirety of both lobes, indicative of extensive past barnacle attachment sites.
localized_surface_anomalies.linear_abrasions: Distinct curvilinear white pixel disruptions (rake-like marks) visible on the inner-mid section of the right lobe and several vertical thin lines on the lower left lobe.

acquired_anomalies_or_scars: Dense clusters of yellowish-white calcified barnacle colonies (Coronula spp.) visible at the extreme distal tips of both the left and right lobes.
other_distinctive_markers: The extreme density of annular scarring creates a unique high-frequency texture across the ventral surface, distinguishing the specimen from standard pigmentation patterns.
